slides.title: OCP's Volunteer Leadership Guide
slides.subtitle: Help people find their place and turn shared effort into useful work.
slides.transcript: A volunteer leader helps people work together. Clear goals, useful feedback, and dependable records make it easier for others to contribute. This guide follows that work from welcoming people to supporting a published contribution.

slides.title: Welcome to OCP volunteer leadership

source_refs.original_title: Welcome to OCP volunteer leadership
source_refs.basis: Original video, figure, captions and transcript preserved unchanged on a media-only slide.

slides.transcript:
The Open Compute Project is a vibrant community

that spans the data center infrastructure worldwide.

Though not a standards body, the OCP Community forges new technology

norms, fostering an ecosystem where industry players collaborate in a safe

framework, shaping a versatile and diverse supply chain.

From startups to hyperscalers, as well as research, academia, and investors,

the OCP Community is able to reduce procurement time, research efforts,

expenses, development time, and even legal complexity for your projects.

Participating in the OCP Community

gives you access to the latest technologies and talent,

the chance to improve your skills, and to drive impact in critical

areas like energy efficiency, cooling, and sustainability.

Join one of the many project workstreams to help solve

challenges and pioneer solutions, or serve as a volunteer leader

to help steer the community towards the industry's ever increasing challenges.

If you're seeking cutting edge solutions, explore our marketplace

or the library of specifications and other contributions,

and embrace OCP solutions in your next endeavor,

or make OCP specifications part of your next RFP.

Check out the latest solutions at an OCP Experience Center, or partner

with any of our OCP recognized facilities or OCP solution providers.

Contribute specifications, design files, reference architectures,

or software, to help solve the industry's

greatest challenges, building trust in you and your brand.

Connect at OCP events through attendance and sponsorship

and embrace OCP’s inclusive open spirit.

Because together we're stronger, faster, and better.

slides.title: Serve the shared purpose

bullets.text: Put the community’s work ahead of company promotion.
Welcome different perspectives and explain decisions.
Help contributors produce useful, shared work.
Keep the five OCP tenets in view.

slides.transcript: Your employer may support your time, but the leadership role serves the community. Welcome different views, explain decisions, and help people create work others can use. OCP’s five tenets provide the common purpose: openness, impact, efficiency, scale, and sustainability.

slides.title: Know your part in the work
slides.transcript: The Steering Committee representative connects the project’s direction with wider OCP goals and contribution decisions. Project Leads organize the charter, plans, calls, and deliverables. Sub-Project Leads guide a technical area within that charter. Workstream Leads coordinate a defined piece of work. Keep goals and progress visible, and agree who decides what. The shared purpose connects all four roles.

slides.transcript: A contribution may be a specification, design package, software, or a document such as a white paper. Tested solutions and other material, including Academy content, have their own routes. The type determines the template, rights, evidence, and review. Help the contributor choose the right one. Published work belongs in the Contribution Database; a draft on a wiki is not yet a published contribution.

slides.title: Three levels of specification
slides.transcript: A Base Specification sets the framework and interfaces. A Design Specification turns requirements into a detailed design. A Product Specification describes the product and its manufacturing implementation. Each adds detail for a different purpose. Agree the template, contribution agreement, and any confidentiality terms before sharing. A contribution does not always need all three layers.

source_refs.basis: Original video, figure, captions and transcript preserved unchanged on a media-only slide.

slides.transcript:
At OCP, our mission is to re-imagine data center, telco, and edge infrastructures

to achieve greater choice, customization and cost savings,

and OCP solution providers play a vital role in making that mission a reality

by delivering and supporting integrated solutions, providing

local engineering architecture resources for customers, establishing

and maintaining relationships with manufacturers of OCP products,

taking part in business planning sessions with the Foundation to better align

with your company's goals,

and of course, actively participating in the OCP Community.

Interested in becoming a solution provider?

The first thing you'll need to do is become an OCP Corporate Member

by signing the appropriate provider agreement and paying the appropriate fee.

The next step is to build

your product based on an approved OCP specification or design package

if you're a colo solution provider,

to complete the OCP Ready colo site assessment.

Once you do, you can enroll your product in the OCP product recognition program for

OCP Accepted approval, or submit your colo facility

site assessment to our incubation committee for OCP Ready recognition.

When your product, solution or facility has been approved, you can get started

marketing your OCP Accepted products, integrated solutions,

or OCP Ready facility on our marketplace and throughout the world.

By participating in the OCP Community as a solution provider,

you have the chance to bring greater efficiencies to your customers’

infrastructure, reach potential adopters, and most importantly,

contribute to reimagining our world's IT infrastructure.

Get started at opencompute.org.

slides.title: Recognize what each program means

cards.title: OCP Accepted™
cards.body: Product alignment with approved OCP work.

cards.title: Experience Center
cards.body: A place to explore equipment and solutions.

slides.transcript: OCP Accepted connects a product to approved OCP work; it does not require disclosure of design files. OCP Ready covers facility self-assessment and approval. Safe covers a defined firmware security review. Experience Centers offer firsthand exploration. The Foundation manages these programs. Leaders can clarify technical questions, but should refer recognition and mark decisions to the program team.

lms_catalog.title: OCP's Volunteer Leadership Guide
lms_catalog.short_description: Help people contribute through clear leadership roles, shared goals, dependable records and useful feedback.
lms_catalog.overview: Volunteer leadership makes it easier for people to work together and create something others can use. Learn how to serve the OCP Community, organize its work and help contributors reach the right reviewers and support.
lms_catalog.duration_note: Includes narration, videos, reading and the final two-question check. Optional close inspection of screenshots and exploration of linked resources may take longer.

modules.summary: Understand the four leadership roles, selection processes, onboarding and shared tools. Connect project goals with meetings, records and useful contributions. Learn how contribution types, specification layers and supporting evidence shape review. Distinguish recognition programs, explore the Marketplace, and guide members to the project, Contribution Hub or Foundation team that can help.
